jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor in Neurobiology & Behavior
jobs.description:
UCI invites applications for a full-time tenure-track Assistant Professor position to join the faculty of the Department of Neurobiology and Behavior in the School of Biological Sciences at the University of California, Irvine.
Ideal applicants will employ rigorous molecular, cellular, circuit, systems, computation, organoid, or behavioral approaches to understand the biological bases of behavior and its disorders, and conduct research that integrates modern neuroscience techniques with conceptually innovative questions. We are specifically interested in candidates whose work addresses addiction and related disorders, including the intersection of social environment with drug use and/or the comorbidity of drug use with other conditions, such as psychiatric disorders, metabolic disease, or infectious disease.
Applicants should hold a Ph.D., M.D.-Ph.D., or equivalent degree(s) and demonstrate evidence for a rigorous research program based on prior research productivity and future research plans. Evidence of securing prior extramural funding will be evaluated positively. Applicants are expected to contribute to teaching at both the graduate and undergraduate levels and demonstrate a commitment to service and leadership at UCI and wider communities.
Please submit a curriculum vitae, 3-page description of research interests and accomplishments, 1-page statement of teaching and mentoring experience, and the contact details for three referees. Information on the department is available at: Neurobiology, UC Irvine Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences.
The successful candidate will be able to leverage and complement existing strengths of the Department of Neurobiology and Behavior, as well as the UCI neuroscience research community including the Irvine Center for Addiction Neuroscience (ICAN), Center for the Study of Cannabis, Institute for Translational Depression Discoveries, Sue & Bill Gross Stem Cell Center, UCI Conte Center, Center for Neural Circuit Mapping, Institute for Memory Impairments and Neurological Disorders, Center for Neurobiology of Learning and Memory, and the Institute for Precision Health.
Department: https://neurobiology.uci.edu/

jobs.title: Computing and Mathematical Sciences Division - Open Rank Faculty Positions in Computer Vision
jobs.institution: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The Computer Vision Area within the Division of Computing and
Mathematical Sciences at MBZUAI invites applications for faculty
positions in computer vision. We welcome candidates in all areas of
computer vision, especially 3D vision and geometric learning,
medical computer vision, multimodal and vision-language models,
video understanding, embodied and robot vision, and Earth
observation. We encourage interdisciplinary collaboration across AI
and related fields. Faculty members will have opportunities to
collaborate with industry partners, government agencies, and
research institutions to develop AI-driven solutions for real-world
challenges.
Faculty responsibilities include teaching, student mentoring, and
curriculum development. Applications are invited at the
Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor levels.
Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) is
a world-leading university dedicated to advancing AI as a global
force for good. The UAE’s visionary leaders established MBZUAI to
educate and develop top talent, conduct advanced research, foster
an innovation ecosystem, and act as a strategic think tank for the
public and private sectors.
The University attracts world-class thinkers and doers in computer
science, AI, bioscience, humanities and beyond. Our groundbreaking
academic research initiatives are developing future solutions that
will impact the world and change the way we imagine things.
Why Join MBZUAI?
Top-Tier Compensation: Competitive salaries aligned with
leading global academic institution
Funding: MBZUAI empowers researchers with resources and
academic freedom, fostering groundbreaking AI advancements in an
environment of innovation and independent inquiry.
Exceptional Benefits:
Comprehensive health & life insurance
Relocation support for international faculty
Build State-of-the-Art Research Facilities: Cutting-edge AI
labs and high-performance computing
Live in Abu Dhabi: World’s safest city, year-round sunshine,
rich culture, and modern amenities
Industry & Government Collaborations: Work with top AI
researchers, leading tech firms, and policymakers
Qualifications
T his position requires a PhD in Computer Vision or a closely
related field. Candidates should have demonstrated excellence in
conducting innovative and impactful research, a strong publication
record in top computer vision and machine learning venues, and an
interest in mentoring students. Candidates at the Associate and
Full Professor levels should also have a record of securing
research funding and leading a research group .
Application Instructions
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until
the positions are filled.
To apply for this position, please submit the following
items:
Cover Letter
Curriculum Vitae
Statement of research vision and interests
Statement of teaching interests, experience, and
philosophy
List of your three most significant publications from the past
five years, and a link to your Google Scholar profile
Reference Letters or Name and contact details for three
referees (Referees will be contacted during the recruitment process
to upload their reference letter via Interfolio).

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Master's in Physician Assistant Studies
jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor - Master's in Physician Assistant
Studies
Grand Rapids, MI (Health Campus)
Full Time
R105173
Grand Valley State University's (GVSU) Master's in Physician
Assistant Studies (MPAS) program welcomes applications for a
full-time, tenure-stream faculty position at its Grand Rapids
location. This full-time tenure-stream faculty position will work
with members of the Physician Assistant Studies (PAS) faculty to
advance the education of PAS students. This position will require
teaching, scholarship, and service responsibilities.
The GVSU MPAS program is recognized for educating first-class
clinicians who are healthcare leaders. We seek a motivated,
energetic individual interested in joining a dedicated and
collaborative faculty. We are committed to upholding the pillars of
inclusion and value the ability to engage effectively with
students, faculty, and staff of diverse backgrounds.
Salary & Benefits:
Minimum starting salary of $105,000; commensurate with
experience
Comprehensive benefits package including medical, vision, dental,
life insurance, generous employer retirement contributions,
wellness resources and tuition waiver effective on date of
hire.
Required Qualifications and Education:
Be (a) an NCCPA-certified physician assistant with a minimum of
a master's degree (PA degree focus), (b) a board-certified (ABMS or
AOA) physician, or (c) an individual with a doctoral degree in a
health-related field. Physician and physician assistant applicants
must be eligible for a Michigan license
Have at least three (3) years of clinical experience if the
applicant meets criteria for (a) or (b) above
Demonstrate leadership and motivational skills and the ability
to work effectively with others
Demonstrate digital literacy appropriate to an academic
environment
Possess a strong commitment to the mission and goals of the
university, college, and Department/Program (www.gvsu.edu; www.gvsu.edu/chp; www.gvsu.edu/pas)
Preferred Qualifications and Education:
Doctoral degree in a related field if applicant meets criteria
for (a) above (e.g., DMSc, DHSc, EdD, PhD)
Two years of teaching experience in higher education,
preferably in a health professions program; clinical precepting
experience will also be considered
Responsibilities - Essential Functions:
Assist with designing, implementing, coordinating, and
evaluating the PAS program curriculum
Develop and revise instructional materials, including lectures,
multimedia content, and online modules, aligned with course
learning outcomes
Serve as course coordinator as needed
Provide lectures, labs, and other educational sessions to
students
Supervise and instruct students in the didactic and/or clinical
year
Evaluate student didactic and clinical performance in
accordance with established competencies, program and course
learning outcomes, instructional objectives, and performance
standards
Assist with making clinical site visits to monitor student
progress and assess the quality of training as needed
Actively participate in the academic advising of PAS program
students to ensure satisfactory progression in achieving PAS
program competencies
Actively participate in ensuring the availability of remedial
instruction to PAS program students as needed
Administrative:
Assist in the admission process, including the recruitment,
application, screening, and selection of students as needed
Assist the Department Chair/Program Director with recruiting,
interviewing, selecting, and developing qualified faculty,
including principal and instructional faculty as needed
Assist the Department Chair/Program Director with recruiting,
interviewing, selecting, and developing Departmental/Program
administrative staff as needed
Coordinate, review, and revise academic policies and procedures
as needed
Develop, review, and revise the PAS program mission, goals, and
competencies as needed
Assist with PAS program evaluation and ongoing
self-assessment
Participate in the assessment of instructional faculty
Assist the Department Chair/Program Director in providing
periodic reports as required and requested to the Dean, College of
Health Professions, University, accrediting agencies, and other
outside agencies
Assist the Department Chair/Program Director in communicating
and cooperating with other departmental chairs and program
directors to promote mutual interests
Promote rapport with local PAs, physicians, and other
healthcare providers
Assist the Department Chair/Program Director and Clinical
Coordinator(s) in working with local agencies to promote the
continual development of clinical training sites and instructional
faculty who serve as supervised clinical experience preceptors
Assist the Department Chair/Program Director and the Clinical
Coordinator(s) in maintaining contact with instructional faculty
who serve as supervised clinical experience preceptors to ensure
the achievement of program educational objectives
Service:
Serve as a member and/or chair of Department/Program, College
of Health Professions, and University committees
Engage in interdepartmental activities that promote the
interest of the program
Attend and participate in Departmental/Program and College of
Health Professions faculty/staff meetings
Attend and participate in Departmental/Program, College of
Health Professions, and University academic and social
functions
Attend meetings of professional organizations and
societies
Participate in state, regional, and national organizations
concerned with the profession to promote a positive image of the PA
concept within the academic, lay, and professional communities
Engage in community activities to promote the PA profession,
encourage increased utilization of PAs, and recruit potential PA
students
Scholarly Activity:
Develop and maintain a scholarship agenda
Disseminate scholarship in both written and oral formats
Integrate evidence-based practice and current research into
teaching and clinical instruction
Participate in collaborative research with colleagues within
the program, across departments, or with community partners
Seek internal and external funding to support scholarly
initiatives when appropriate
Miscellaneous:
Participate in ongoing self-assessment to promote development,
service, and scholarly activities
Remain clinically active and current in the practice of
medicine, where applicable
How to Apply: Apply online at jobs.gvsu.edu and select "Apply
now". Include a cover letter, CV/resume, and contact information
for three references. The online application will allow you to
attach these documents electronically. Applicants selected for
interviews will be required to submit official transcripts prior to
the interview. If you need assistance, please contact the Search
Committee Chair, Katie Aurand, at trestonk@gvsu.edu or Human
Resources at HRO@gvsu.edu or 616-331-2215.
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States
and must not require sponsorship now or in the future.
Application Deadline:
Application review begins December 15, 2026. This posting may be
closed at any time at the discretion of the University.
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to
perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Must have the physical
stamina to work long hours and/or more than 5 days per week. The
requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill
and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to
enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential
functions. The information contained in this job description is for
compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act as amended by
the ADA Amendment Act (2008), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act
of 1973, and other applicable federal and state laws that prohibit
discrimination on the basis of disability. GVSU will provide
reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with
disabilities upon request. See www.gvsu.edu/equalopportunity/. TDD
Callers: Call Michigan Relay Center at 711 (in State) or
1-800-833-7833 (out of State).
Grand Valley State University is an Antidiscrimination/Equal
Opportunity Employer, which includes providing equal opportunity
for protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.
University policy extends protections to additional
identities.
To apply, visit https://gvsu.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/careers/job/Grand-Rapids-MI-Health-Campus/Assistant-Professor---Master-s-in-Physician-Assistant-Studies_R105173

jobs.title: Assistant Professor- Biomedical Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor- Biomedical Engineering
Job Description Summary, Duties and Responsibilities, Required
Qualifications and Preferred Qualifications
Search will be open until filled. First
consideration will be given to applications received by December
31, 2026. Applications received after December 31, 2026 may be
reviewed depending on search progress and needs but are not
guaranteed full consideration.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________
About URI:
The University of Rhode Island enrolls
approximately 17,000 students across its graduate and undergraduate
programs and is the State's flagship public research university, as
well as the land grant and sea grant university, for the state of
Rhode Island. The main campus is located in the historic village of
Kingston, and the Bay Campus is located in Narragansett. Both
campuses are near major beaches in a beautiful coastal community.
URI is just 30 minutes from Providence, RI and within easy reach of
Newport, Boston, and New York City.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________
A Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering or a closely related field is
required at the time of appointment.
Applications are invited for a tenure-track Assistant Professor
position in the Department of Biomedical Engineering, beginning in
Fall 2027. We are particularly interested in candidates developing
innovative technologies and computational approaches to understand,
monitor, restore, or enhance human health and function. Areas of
interest include, but are not limited to, biomechanics,
biomaterials, rehabilitation technologies,
robotics, bioinstrumentation, biosensors, wearable technologies,
neuroprosthetics and assistive technologies, medical imaging,
biomedical signal processing, AI-driven immersive technologies and
biomedical big data.
The Department of Biomedical Engineering at the University of Rhode
Island (URI) became an independent department within the College of
Engineering in the 2026 academic year, following a long history as
a program within the Department of Electrical, Computer, and
Biomedical Engineering. As part of this transition, the
undergraduate curriculum was revised to establish three primary
tracks: Bioinstrumentation and Neural Engineering, Biomechanics and
Prosthetics, and Biomedical AI. Biomedical Engineering currently
offers a B.S. degree and partners with the Department of Electrical
and Computer Engineering to offer M.S. and Ph.D. degrees. The
Department is currently developing independent M.S. and Ph.D.
programs.
Our BME faculty conduct research in neural signal processing,
neuro-instrumentation, neuro-robotics, neuromodulation, wearable
health systems, digital health, medical imaging and signal
processing, physiological modeling, biomedical AI and machine
learning, and assistive and rehabilitation technologies. The
interdisciplinary nature of the Department provides faculty with
opportunities to collaborate with colleagues across the University.
A recently inaugurated 195,000-square-foot engineering building
provides an excellent environment for interdisciplinary research
and collaboration.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________
THE POSITION IS ELIGIBLE FOR A HYBRID WORK
SCHEDULE
POSITION SUMMARY:
Develop and teach undergraduate and graduate courses
while establishing a high-quality research program in biomedical
engineering.
The successful candidate will have opportunities to
collaborate with faculty in Electrical and Computer Engineering,
Communicative Disorders, Kinesiology, Physical Therapy, Nursing,
Computer Science and Statistics, Biomedical and Pharmaceutical
Sciences, and beyond. These opportunities will continue to expand

partners in the Providence and Boston areas.

jobs.institution: University of Texas at San Antonio
jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor, Film and Media Studies, Interdisciplinary
School for Engagement
Location: San Antonio, TX
Regular/Temporary: Regular
Job ID: 16710
Full/Part Time: Full Time
Position Information
Assistant Professor in Film &
Media Studies for the Interdisciplinary School for
Engagement
The University of Texas at San Antonio
Interdisciplinary School for Engagement invites applications for a
tenure-track Assistant Professor in Film & Media Studies.
The University of Texas at San
Antonio
The University of Texas at San
Antonio (UT San Antonio) is a nationally recognized,
top-tier public research university that unites the power of higher
education, biomedical discovery and healthcare within one visionary
institution. As the third-largest research university in Texas and
a Carnegie R1-designated institution, UT San Antonio is a model of
access and excellence — advancing knowledge, social mobility and
public health across South Texas and beyond. UT San Antonio serves
approximately 42,000 students in 320 academic programs spanning
science, engineering, medicine, health, liberal arts, AI,
cybersecurity, business, education and more. With 17,000 faculty
and staff, UT San Antonio has also been recognized as a Top
Employer in Texas by Forbes Magazine. Learn more online, on UT San Antonio Today or on
X, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube or
LinkedIn.
College of Liberal and Fine
Arts
The Interdisciplinary School for Engagement is
housed within the College of Liberal and Fine Arts (COLFA). COLFA
is on an accelerated trajectory of transformation and growth fueled
by three major drivers: reimagining the humanities, recommitting to
arts education, and bolstering social science research. In line
with these initiatives, the College recently established the School
for Interdisciplinary Engagement, designed to further collaborative
engagement and discovery around the intersections of grand
challenges facing society and the human experience. We envision the
person in this new position building bridges among these areas
while engaging with UT San Antonio's strengths in community
engagement, healthcare, business, artificial intelligence, and data
science.
The Interdisciplinary School for
Engagement
The Interdisciplinary School for Engagement
(ISE) in the College of Liberal and Fine Arts at UT San Antonio
houses five undergraduate majors and seven minors as well as an MFA
in Film and Media. It consists of more than 25 tenure/tenure track
and fixed-term-track faculty members serving more than 850
students. Given its unique mission, the ISE serves as a home for
interdisciplinary programs as well as a makerspace and intellectual
incubator for new programs in the humanities and social sciences.
It is also committed to provide space for collaborative learning
and teaching and engage our students in experiential learning and
discovery.
Salary Range: Competitive,
commensurate with education, experience, and qualifications.
Job Type: Full Time
Position Summary
The Interdisciplinary School for Engagement
(ISE) in the College of Liberal and Fine Arts at UT San Antonio
invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Film
and Media Studies beginning in Fall 2027. We are interested in
areas of specialization that focus on the intersections of media,
community engagement, and scholarship.
Review of applications begins four weeks after
posting went online and continues until the position is filled. The
course load in the School is typically two courses per semester
(2/2). The School offers the new assistant professor a competitive
startup funding package for the first year and typically two course
releases during the first three years.
Core Responsibilities
Teaching courses in Film History, Film Theory, and other
courses within Film and Media Studies at both the undergraduate and
graduate levels.
Developing curricula, teaching, and supervising theses or
serving on thesis committees at the graduate level.
Maintaining an active research agenda that contributes to
program strengths in community engagement, curation, and public
humanities.
Publishing scholarly work in appropriate peer-reviewed outlets
and presenting research at professional and scholarly conferences,
or producing creative research equivalent in intellectual
impact.
Pursuing interdisciplinary research and external funding
opportunities as appropriate to the candidate's research
agenda.
Mentoring and advising undergraduate and graduate students,
including on bilingual scholarly or creative projects.
Participating in appropriate School, College, University,
professional, and community service.
Taking on leadership positions in a growing, community-engaged
program.
This position may require the ability to maintain the security
and integrity of UT San Antonio and its infrastructure per Texas
EO-GA-48.
Required Qualifications
Ph.D. in a related field.
The candidate must show evidence of a strong scholarly research
background in Media Studies, with a specific emphasis in topics
relevant to Texas and/or Latin America or to existing
Interdisciplinary programs within the school, especially Media
& Medicine or Community Arts.
Preferred Qualifications
University teaching experience, a record of service, and
evidence of creative/scholarly contributions to the field.
History of invited contributions and speaking engagements,
awards or commissions, media hits, and similar that demonstrate
scholarly/creative reputation.
History of leadership related to major curation, outreach,
education, or program-building activities that engage academic and
community members with Film/Media Studies and/or Media Arts.
Demonstrated familiarity with the historical and current media
landscape of film and media in Texas and San Antonio, where recent
investments by local and state government are likely to have
dramatic impact on student recruitment and experiential
opportunities, as well as impact on community engagement with and
understanding of film and media.
Expertise in media studies fields relevant to Texas and/or
Latin America.
Experience pursuing external funding or demonstrated potential
to develop externally funded research.
Experience with experiential, community-engaged, or applied
teaching and scholarship, including creation or curation of major
initiatives with significant impacts on communities internal and
external to the academy.
Application Process
To apply, applicants must upload the following
in a single PDF document:
Letter of application that includes research interests,
teaching experiences, and qualifications for the position.
Current curriculum vitae (CV).
Copy of graduate transcripts.
Samples of written or published scholarly work (no more than
three).
Two representative samples of syllabi for immediately relevant
courses taught by the applicant.
List of three references (including name, title, institution,
telephone number and email address) familiar with the applicant's
work.
Screening of completed applications will begin
immediately and continue until position is filled. Applicants must
apply by November 30, 2026, on the UT San
Antonio Career Site.
Posting Close Date:
Applications will be accepted through 11:59 PM CDT on 11/30/2026.
At the discretion of the hiring department, this posting may close
once a sufficient number of qualified applications have been
received.
This position
will work primarily on campus. Travel and parking
expenses are the employee's responsibility.
This position
is contingent upon a successful background check. Verification of a
valid driver's license and Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) may be
completed as applicable. Applicants selected must be able to show
proof of eligibility to work in the United States by time of
hire.
Equal
Employment Opportunity
As an equal
employment opportunity and affirmative action employer, it is the
policy of The University of Texas at San Antonio to promote and
ensure equal employment opportunity for all individuals regardless
of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation,
national origin, age, disability or genetic information, and
veteran status. The University is committed to the Affirmative
Action Program in compliance with all government requirements to
ensure nondiscrimination.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Japanese
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor of Japanese
College: College of Humanities, Social Sciences, and The
Arts - 321 College
Dept/School: World Languages and Cultures - 32221
Vacancy Number: 16F-828
Position Number: 618
Location of Workplace: Main UNCW Campus
Brief Summary of Work for this Position:
The Department of World Languages and Cultures at the University of
North Carolina Wilmington seeks applications for a tenure-track
position as Assistant Professor of Japanese to begin August
2027.
The Japanese program at UNCW is currently small but over capacity,
with high student interest and enrollment demonstrating a potential
for growth. We seek a candidate with exceptional language teaching
capability and a vision for contributing to continued program
development, with the goal of demonstrating the value of Japanese
study to the university and students. Teaching responsibilities
include a regular research-intensive load of five courses per
year.
The successful candidate will teach Japanese language and culture
courses, work together with the Japanese minor program coordinator
to offer study abroad programs in Japan, advise students and
relevant student organizations, collaborate with related programs,
produce scholarship, and provide department and university
service.
The successful candidate will be responsible for at least one
course on an aspect of contemporary Japanese language, culture, or
society (e.g. arts and entertainment, business and finance,
demographic challenges, politics, sociolinguistics, technology,
tourism and recreation, and so on). The research area is thus open
to all candidates who can demonstrate how their research
contributes to potential growth in the Japanese minor and the
Japanese program broadly.
The successful candidate is expected to be an expert in Japanese
language pedagogy from the beginning to upper-intermediate levels
of proficiency. Special consideration will be given to candidates
with the demonstrated ability to build connections with other
academic, extracurricular, or community-based programs.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:
PhD or EdD in the field of Japanese language and culture, or
closely related discipline (such as Second Language Acquisition or
Asian Studies, with at least 18 graduate credit hours in Japanese
language, literature, culture, pedagogy, etc.)
Please note: ABD applicants will be
considered; however, if PhD or EdD is not confirmed by
August 1, 2027, appointment will be at the rank of Lecturer for the
first academic year of employment and PhD must be confirmed by July
1, 2028 for eligibility of continued employment. In addition, one
of the references included in application must be dissertation
chair.
Excellent oral and written communication skills in Japanese and
English
Evidence of an active research agenda
Potential to contribute to courses in the Japanese minor
Experience teaching Japanese as a foreign language at the
university level
Preferred Education, Knowledge, Skills &
Experience:
Experience developing and/or teaching courses in Japanese
contemporary culture, language and society, or Japanese for
specific purposes including business
Experience with leading or developing study abroad programs,
internships, work opportunities for Japanese learners, or
community-based partnerships
Required Certifications or Licensure:
Primary Function of Organizational Unit:
The Department of World Languages and Cultures in the College of
Humanities, Social Sciences, and Arts is one of the largest
academic units at the University of North Carolina Wilmington. With
over 50 faculty members, we offer on-campus and online master's
degrees in Spanish; on-campus and online post-baccalaureate
certificates in Hispanic Studies; a combined BA/MA program in
Spanish; bachelor's degrees in French, German, and Spanish; and
minors in Classics, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese, Spanish,
and Russian. We also offer classes in American Sign Language,
Arabic, and Italian.
College/School Information:
The College of Humanities, Social Sciences, and the Arts (CHSSA) is
home to 14 academic departments and offers a wide variety of
undergraduate and graduate degree programs including the Bachelor
of Arts, Bachelor of Fine Arts, Bachelor of Music, Master of Arts,
Master of Fine Arts, and Master of Public Administration as well as
combined bachelor's/master's degree programs in Spanish and
English. CHSSA also houses the Interdisciplinary Studies
program(s), Gender Studies and Research Center and the Academic
Resource Center, which offers full-service, professional advising
for all CHSSA undergraduate students.
In addition, CHSSA offers a full complement of interdisciplinary
minors and post baccalaureate certificates including: Africana
studies, American studies, Asian studies, classical studies,
conflict management and resolution, emergency and disaster
management, forensic science, Hispanic studies, journalism, Latin
American studies, medical humanities, Middle East and Islamic
studies, Native American studies, professional writing and
publishing, science and medical writing, and women's, gender, and
sexuality studies.
CHSSA contributes significantly to the curriculum that comprises
UNCW's University Studies Program, through which all undergraduates
gain a foundation in the liberal arts and develop the transferable
skills essential for life in the twenty-first century. CHSSA
strives in its undergraduate programs and in its University Study
offerings to nurture creative thinking, intellectual curiosity, and
academic integrity in students while providing them with a solid
foundation of knowledge in their chosen fields. Graduate programs
in CHSSA are designed to develop intellectual competence and to
prepare the student for careers in business, industry, government,
teaching or for further study at the doctoral level.
Applied learning is a hallmark of the student experience in CHSSA.
Each of CHSSA's departments requires an applied learning experience
as a part of the curriculum for its undergraduate majors. Examples
include faculty-directed research, internships, service learning,
and capstone courses and projects, all of which challenge students
to integrate various strands of knowledge and to apply that
knowledge to broader, real-world or real disciplinary
situations.
Upon completion of their studies, all CHSSA students will have the
necessary preparation for rewarding careers, advanced study,
effective citizenship, and meaningful lives. CHSSA offers limitless
opportunities to engage in collaborative and interdisciplinary
research and service while also making a positive societal impact.
Come and join our vibrant academic environment that values
discovery, innovation, and creativity.
University Information:
The University of North Carolina Wilmington, the state's coastal
university, is dedicated to the integration of teaching, mentoring,
research and service. Widely acknowledged for its world-class
faculty and staff and continuously recognized at a national level
for scholarly excellence and affordability, UNCW offers a powerful
academic experience that stimulates creative inquiry and critical
thinking.
A public institution with nearly 18,000 students, UNCW offers a
full range of baccalaureate- and graduate-level programs, as well
as doctoral degrees in educational leadership, marine biology,
nursing practice and psychology; and many distance learning
options, including clinical research, an accelerated RN-to-BSN
program, an Executive M.B.A. program structured for working
professionals, and the nation's only bachelor's degree program
focused on coastal engineering.
The university's efforts to advance research and scholarly
activities have earned UNCW the elevated designation of "Doctoral
Universities: High Research Activity" institution (R2 University)
by the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher
Education.
UNCW has been part of the University of North Carolina System since
1969.
Eligibility for Employment:
Final candidates are subject to criminal & sex offender
background checks. Some vacancies also require credit or motor
vehicle checks. UNC Wilmington participates in E-Verify. Federal
law requires all employers to verify the identity and employment
eligibility of all persons hired to work in the United
States.
Number of Openings: Single Incumbent
Special Notes to Applicants:
Prior to the official appointment to the university, the candidate
selected for hire must be able to demonstrate eligibility to teach
assigned courses by successfully meeting the credentialing
requirements based on official transcripts and other documentation
as required.
Applications will be accepted until 11:59PM EST on the posting
closing date. To apply, please complete the online application
available at https://jobs.uncw.edu/ and attach the
following required materials as Adobe PDF documents:
Cover Letter
Curriculum Vita
Combined Unofficial Graduate Transcripts
Research Summary/Statement of Research Plans (1-2 pages)
Teaching Philosophy (1-2 pages)
Additional materials may be requested from applicants invited to
interview for the position.
Please note that a minimum of three references are required for all
applications. Note:. If ABD at time at application one of the
references included in application must be dissertation
chair.
The reference contact information you provide may be used to
request reference letters during the screening process.
Questions about the position or the online application process
should be directed to CHSSA Recruitment Specialist Jennifer Itell @
itellj@uncw.edu.

jobs.title: Regional Faculty Director for Admissions and Student Affairs
jobs.description:
Regional Faculty Director for Admissions and Student
Affairs
Details
Position/Rank Regional Faculty Director
Department Division of Medical Education
City St. George, UT
Track Non Tenure Track
New Position to Begin When filled
Details
Utah has the ninth lowest number of physicians and the lowest
number of primary care physicians per capita in the United States.
Utah's physician workforce does not meet the state's needs,
particularly in rural communities. The Spencer Fox Eccles School of
Medicine (SFESOM) at the University of Utah is seeking a dynamic
and experienced leader to join the administrative leadership team
at the Southern Utah Regional Medical Campus (SURMC) in St. George,
Utah. The SURMC will increase the number of medical student
graduates pursuing careers in rural medicine, with a focus on
primary care and other high-need generalist fields. A class of 10
medical students per year—the Southern Utah cohort—will begin their
educational experiences at the SURMC in Fall 2027, after completing
Phase 1 (2026-27) of a new mission-driven MD program on the
University of Utah campus in Salt Lake City. All SURMC students are
SFESOM Rural Medicine Scholars (RMS) alongside 10 additional
medical students per year based in Salt Lake City who complete a
longitudinal clinical training experience at other rural sites
across Utah and the Mountain West.
Job Summary
The SURMC Regional Faculty Director of Admissions and Student
Affairs (RFDASA) collaborates with faculty and staff to design and
implement innovative strategies for outreach, selection, and
evaluation of future SURMC students, collaborating on admissions
processes that reflect the SFESOM's mission and values. Once
admitted, the RFDASA works directly with medical students to
facilitate their academic growth, personal wellness, and
professional identity formation. The RFDASA provides leadership and
mentorship to the SURMC Admissions and Student Affairs staff teams.
The RFDASA supports the University of Utah's goals and mission and
acts as a catalyst between departments, faculty, staff, students,
and external entities.
The SURMC RFDSA will report directly to the Associate Dean of
SURMC. As a rural regional campus of the SFESOM, the RFDASA also
collaborates closely with the Associate and Assistant Deans of
Student Affairs, the Assistant Dean of Admissions, and the Senior
Associate Dean of Rural, Underserved, and Regional Medical
Education. This newly created position holds salary support of 0.25
FTE and is an adjunct appointment in the Division of Medical
Education. Salary will be set for the administrative effort based
on benchmarks utilized for other senior administrative leaders in
the SFESOM Dean's Office. Academic rank will be commensurate with
education and experience.
Roles & Responsibilities
● Develops and implements a vision for SURMC admissions and student
affairs programming in partnership with Salt Lake and regional
campus leadership to ensure alignment with SFESOM mission and
educational goals across campuses.
● Partners with Office of Admissions, SURMC, and RMS program
leadership, faculty, and staff to oversee all aspects of the RMS
admissions process, of which the SURMC is a part, ensuring
recruitment and selection of exceptional candidates for the
regional campus and the RMS program overall, and full compliance
with internal policies and accreditation-related, regulatory, and
legal standards.
● Represents SFESOM, RMS, and SURMC admissions to internal and
external parties, including University offices, local/regional
partners, national medical education consortia, accrediting bodies,
and application services.
● Supports applicant screening for the RMS program.
● Co-chairs the RMS selection committee with a Salt Lake City
campus counterpart, and supports staff in the recruitment,
training, and evaluation of its members.
● Serves as a SURMC and RMS program spokesperson for the SFESOM
medical education program to premedical advisors, educational
institutions, and the broader academic community, strengthening
relationships that support recruitment and outreach.
● Develops programs to ensure appropriate support for SURMC
students in the areas of student wellness, academic success, course
scheduling, financial aid, student records and transcripts,
visiting student experiences, and the residency match
process.
● Meets individually with all SURMC students at least once a year
to review their academic progress, personal wellness, professional
identity formation, specialty decision making and match
process.
● Participates in the attempts to eradicate medical student
mistreatment including reviewing mistreatment reports as assigned,
tracking and categorizing mistreatment events, and meeting with
clinical departments to report mistreatment events.
● Participates in the creation of the yearly Medical Student
Performance Evaluation (MSPE) for SURMC students.
● Participates as a representative of Student Affairs and
Admissions in other Dean's Office wide committees such as the
Education Program and Policy Committee (EPPC), Academic Readiness
Committee (ARC), and other University committees as needed.
● Participates in a variety of community building events within the
house model and SURMC campus to build strong relationships with
students.
● Other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
● Advanced medicine degree (MD or DO) required.
● Completion of an ACGME-accredited residency.
● Eligibility for an unrestricted Utah physician and surgeon
license (see DOPL requirements).
● Demonstrated leadership experience, with excellent interpersonal
and communication skills, and the ability to work with various
stakeholders in the SFESOM.
● Strong experience in medical education and medical student
support services and contemporary knowledge of the culture of
academic medicine, the challenges in the Match Process (UME to GME
transition), and the issues of wellness, diversity, academic
performance that medical students face is preferred.
How to Apply
Interested candidates should submit an abbreviated curriculum vitae
highlighting experience relevant to the position (3 pages or less),
cover letter (1 page or less), and names and contact information of
three professional references. Applications will be reviewed upon
receipt. Please contact Reed Nelson for additional information or
questions.
All applications must be submitted online at: https://utah.peopleadmin.com/postings/208262
Inquiries may be directed to:
Reed Nelson, MD, MPH, Associate Dean, Southern Utah Regional
Medical Campus
Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine at the University of
Utah
reed.nelson@hsc.utah.edu

jobs.title: Clinical Assistant Professor, Child Life & Family-Centered Care
jobs.institution: Boston University Wheelock College of Education & Human Development
jobs.description:
Clinical Assistant Professor, Child Life & Family-Centered Care
Boston University Wheelock College of Education & Human Development invites applications for a full-time Clinical Assistant Professor in Child Life and Family-Centered Care. The MS Child Life and Family-Centered Care program is the oldest, and most respected, academic Child Life program in the United States. It was the first graduate program in the country to be endorsed by the Association of Child Life Professionals (ACLP). We seek candidates with a background in child life, who are ready to assume a leadership role in the program, teach and supervise students in clinical child life internships, and expand an agenda for psychosocial and child life research. Candidates should have the knowledge and experience to teach child life courses and have the ability to teach one or more family-centered care courses, such as bereavement care, working with parents, and lifespan development.
The Counseling Psychology and Applied Human Development Department, where the Child Life and Family-Centered Care program is housed, believes that the cultural and social diversity of our faculty, staff, and students is vitally important to the distinction and excellence of our research and academic programs. We encourage applicants who support our institutional commitment to equity, diversity, and belonging and to being an inclusive university where all constituents can thrive. Competitive candidates will demonstrate a background of engaged and collaborative scholarship, practice, and teaching, as well as a commitment to curricula to reflect on the unique histories, experiences, and challenges faced by marginalized individuals.
Since its founding in 1839, Boston University has embraced a mission of openness and access, becoming one of the first universities in the nation to welcome all students of ability regardless of race, gender, or creed. That tradition shapes our enduring commitment to academic freedom, free inquiry, and the robust exchange of ideas. Please visit https://www.bu.edu/values/ to learn more about our shared values.
We seek scholars who will contribute to our community of teachers and researchers through excellence in innovative scholarship, engaged teaching, and participation in the intellectual life of the University. Boston University provides an environment where faculty and students work together across disciplines, perspectives, and experiences to advance knowledge and address society’s most pressing challenges.
Responsibilities
Teach courses related to our master’s degree program in child life
Maintain a strong program of grant-funded research
Supervise graduate students in practicum placements and independent research.
Be an engaged citizen in providing service to the department, college, university, and the profession.
Required Qualifications
Earned doctorate in child development, human development and family studies, or a related field
Certification as a Child Life Specialist through the Association of Child Life Professionals
Experience with supervision of Child Life students
An active and coherent program of research
Established record of teaching courses in child life or related fields
Training in and experience providing child life internship placements
Preferred Qualifications
Child Life program leadership experience
Experience across multiple clinical settings or patient populations

Salary Range
The expected base pay range for this position is $100,000 - $110,000. This base pay range is for a nine-month academic appointment. Additional compensation up to three months may be earned for activities including but not limited to funded research and summer teaching.
The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to departmental budgets, qualifications, experience, education, licenses, specialty, training and internal pay comparison. The above hiring range represents the University's good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting.
